inputs.name: Worden bound
inputs.value: O(1) bits per generation, constant unspecified
inputs.cite: H4 q1 (Day's paraphrase; Worden 1995 not retrieved)

day.reading: Worden's O(1) bits per generation is exactly the same as the Haldane-scale limit
day.holds: both are O(1)-scale ceilings on adaptive change, and they coincide if a substitution carries about 300 bits

critic.reading: the equivalence needs a bits-per-substitution conversion the post does not give
critic.holds: equality holds only at b = 300c; at one bit per substitution the information limit is 300x faster; Haldane counts deaths (30 N), Worden counts bits

notes: Units only. O(1) bits per generation equals 1/300 substitutions per generation only when each substitution carries 300c bits, with c the unstated constant; nothing in the quoted sentence or the held paraphrase fixes c or b. At b = 1 the information bound allows 300 times the Haldane rate. 'Exactly the same' is therefore a conditional equivalence. Worden 1995 is not retrieved, so the bound's own derivation is not checked here.
